118: // Tokenize takes bytes as input and lexes it into
119: // a list of tokens that can be parsed as a Caddyfile.
120: // Also takes a filename to fill the token's File as
121: // the source of the tokens, which is important to
122: // determine relative paths for `import` directives.
123: func Tokenize(input []byte, filename string) ([]Token, error) {
124: 	l := lexer{}
125: 	if err := l.load(bytes.NewReader(input)); err != nil {
126: 		return nil, err
127: 	}
128: 	var tokens []Token
129: 	for {
130: 		found, err := l.next()
131: 		if err != nil {
132: 			return nil, err
133: 		}
134: 		if !found {
135: 			break
136: 		}
137: 		l.token.File = filename
138: 		tokens = append(tokens, l.token)
139: 	}
140: 	return tokens, nil
141: }

143: // load prepares the lexer to scan an input for tokens.
144: // It discards any leading byte order mark.
145: func (l *lexer) load(input io.Reader) error {
146: 	l.reader = bufio.NewReader(input)
147: 	l.line = 1
148: 
149: 	// discard byte order mark, if present
150: 	firstCh, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
151: 	if err != nil {
152: 		return err
153: 	}
154: 	if firstCh != 0xFEFF {
155: 		err := l.reader.UnreadRune()
156: 		if err != nil {
157: 			return err
158: 		}
159: 	}
160: 
161: 	return nil
162: }

164: // next loads the next token into the lexer.
165: // A token is delimited by whitespace, unless
166: // the token starts with a quotes character (")
167: // in which case the token goes until the closing
168: // quotes (the enclosing quotes are not included).
169: // Inside quoted strings, quotes may be escaped
170: // with a preceding \ character. No other chars
171: // may be escaped. The rest of the line is skipped
172: // if a "#" character is read in. Returns true if
173: // a token was loaded; false otherwise.
174: func (l *lexer) next() (bool, error) {
175: 	var val []rune
176: 	var comment, quoted, btQuoted, inHeredoc, heredocEscaped, escaped bool
177: 	var heredocMarker string
178: 
179: 	makeToken := func(quoted rune) bool {
180: 		l.token.Text = string(val)
181: 		l.token.wasQuoted = quoted
182: 		l.token.heredocMarker = heredocMarker
183: 		return true
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	for {
187: 		// Read a character in; if err then if we had
188: 		// read some characters, make a token. If we
189: 		// reached EOF, then no more tokens to read.
190: 		// If no EOF, then we had a problem.
191: 		ch, _, err := l.reader.ReadRune()
192: 		if err != nil {
193: 			if len(val) > 0 {
194: 				if inHeredoc {
195: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("incomplete heredoc <<%s on line #%d, expected ending marker %s", heredocMarker, l.line+l.skippedLines, heredocMarker)
196: 				}
197: 
198: 				return makeToken(0), nil
199: 			}
200: 			if err == io.EOF {
201: 				return false, nil
202: 			}
203: 			return false, err
204: 		}
205: 
206: 		// detect whether we have the start of a heredoc
207: 		if !inHeredoc && !heredocEscaped && len(val) > 1 && string(val[:2]) == "<<" {
208: 			if ch == '<' {
209: 				return false, fmt.Errorf("too many '<' for heredoc on line #%d; only use two, for example <<END", l.line)
210: 			}
211: 			if ch == '\r' {
212: 				continue
213: 			}
214: 			// after hitting a newline, we know that the heredoc marker
215: 			// is the characters after the two << and the newline.
216: 			// we reset the val because the heredoc is syntax we don't
217: 			// want to keep.
218: 			if ch == '\n' {
219: 				heredocMarker = string(val[2:])
220: 				if !heredocMarkerRegexp.Match([]byte(heredocMarker)) {
221: 					return false, fmt.Errorf("heredoc marker on line #%d must contain only alpha-numeric characters, dashes and underscores; got '%s'", l.line, heredocMarker)
222: 				}
223: 
224: 				inHeredoc = true
225: 				l.skippedLines++
226: 				val = nil
227: 				continue
228: 			}
229: 			val = append(val, ch)
230: 			continue
231: 		}
232: 
233: 		// if we're in a heredoc, all characters are read as-is
234: 		if inHeredoc {
235: 			val = append(val, ch)
236: 
237: 			if ch == '\n' {
238: 				l.skippedLines++
239: 			}
240: 
241: 			// check if we're done, i.e. that the last few characters are the marker
242: 			if len(val) > len(heredocMarker) && heredocMarker == string(val[len(val)-len(heredocMarker):]) {
243: 				// set the final value
244: 				val, err = l.finalizeHeredoc(val, heredocMarker)
245: 				if err != nil {
246: 					return false, err
247: 				}
248: 
249: 				// set the line counter, and make the token
250: 				l.line += l.skippedLines
251: 				l.skippedLines = 0
252: 				return makeToken('<'), nil
253: 			}
254: 
255: 			// stay in the heredoc until we find the ending marker
256: 			continue
257: 		}
258: 
259: 		// track whether we found an escape '\' for the next
260: 		// iteration to be contextually aware
261: 		if !escaped && !btQuoted && ch == '\\' {
262: 			escaped = true
263: 			continue
264: 		}
265: 
266: 		if quoted || btQuoted {
267: 			if quoted && escaped {
268: 				// all is literal in quoted area,
269: 				// so only escape quotes
270: 				if ch != '"' {
271: 					val = append(val, '\\')
272: 				}
273: 				escaped = false
274: 			} else {
275: 				if (quoted && ch == '"') || (btQuoted && ch == '`') {
276: 					return makeToken(ch), nil
277: 				}
278: 			}
279: 			// allow quoted text to wrap continue on multiple lines
280: 			if ch == '\n' {
281: 				l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
282: 				l.skippedLines = 0
283: 			}
284: 			// collect this character as part of the quoted token
285: 			val = append(val, ch)
286: 			continue
287: 		}
288: 
289: 		if unicode.IsSpace(ch) {
290: 			// ignore CR altogether, we only actually care about LF (\n)
291: 			if ch == '\r' {
292: 				continue
293: 			}
294: 			// end of the line
295: 			if ch == '\n' {
296: 				// newlines can be escaped to chain arguments
297: 				// onto multiple lines; else, increment the line count
298: 				if escaped {
299: 					l.skippedLines++
300: 					escaped = false
301: 				} else {
302: 					l.line += 1 + l.skippedLines
303: 					l.skippedLines = 0
304: 				}
305: 				// comments (#) are single-line only
306: 				comment = false
307: 			}
308: 			// any kind of space means we're at the end of this token
309: 			if len(val) > 0 {
310: 				return makeToken(0), nil
311: 			}
312: 			continue
313: 		}
314: 
315: 		// comments must be at the start of a token,
316: 		// in other words, preceded by space or newline
317: 		if ch == '#' && len(val) == 0 {
318: 			comment = true
319: 		}
320: 		if comment {
321: 			continue
322: 		}
323: 
324: 		if len(val) == 0 {
325: 			l.token = Token{Line: l.line}
326: 			if ch == '"' {
327: 				quoted = true
328: 				continue
329: 			}
330: 			if ch == '`' {
331: 				btQuoted = true
332: 				continue
333: 			}
334: 		}
335: 
336: 		if escaped {
337: 			// allow escaping the first < to skip the heredoc syntax
338: 			if ch == '<' {
339: 				heredocEscaped = true
340: 			} else {
341: 				val = append(val, '\\')
342: 			}
343: 			escaped = false
344: 		}
345: 
346: 		val = append(val, ch)
347: 	}
348: }

350: // finalizeHeredoc takes the runes read as the heredoc text and the marker,
351: // and processes the text to strip leading whitespace, returning the final
352: // value without the leading whitespace.
353: func (l *lexer) finalizeHeredoc(val []rune, marker string) ([]rune, error) {
354: 	stringVal := string(val)
355: 
356: 	// find the last newline of the heredoc, which is where the contents end
357: 	lastNewline := strings.LastIndex(stringVal, "\n")
358: 
359: 	// collapse the content, then split into separate lines
360: 	lines := strings.Split(stringVal[:lastNewline+1], "\n")
361: 
362: 	// figure out how much whitespace we need to strip from the front of every line
363: 	// by getting the string that precedes the marker, on the last line
364: 	paddingToStrip := stringVal[lastNewline+1 : len(stringVal)-len(marker)]
365: 
366: 	// iterate over each line and strip the whitespace from the front
367: 	var out string
368: 	for lineNum, lineText := range lines[:len(lines)-1] {
369: 		// find an exact match for the padding
370: 		index := strings.Index(lineText, paddingToStrip)
371: 
372: 		// if the padding doesn't match exactly at the start then we can't safely strip
373: 		if index != 0 {
374: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("mismatched leading whitespace in heredoc <<%s on line #%d [%s], expected whitespace [%s] to match the closing marker", marker, l.line+lineNum+1, lineText, paddingToStrip)
375: 		}
376: 
377: 		// strip, then append the line, with the newline, to the output.
378: 		// also removes all "\r" because Windows.
379: 		out += strings.ReplaceAll(lineText[len(paddingToStrip):]+"\n", "\r", "")
380: 	}
381: 
382: 	// Remove the trailing newline from the loop
383: 	if len(out) > 0 && out[len(out)-1] == '\n' {
384: 		out = out[:len(out)-1]
385: 	}
386: 
387: 	// return the final value
388: 	return []rune(out), nil
389: }
